transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Recording: Fireflies auto transcript (medium quality)
Attendees: Jordan Li (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood Partner Lead); Priya Nair (Oceanic Head Partnerships), Ethan Morales (Sales Ops), Dr. Lena Zhou (CTO), Amir Khan (Solutions Architect)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/partner-deck (deck v2), internal playbook link (redwood_intra/partners/cosell_v2 - noted), RetailPilot brief (link redacted)

Summary:
Quick, candid retrospective of co-sell trials to date, focus on improving intake/crediting, clarifying Dedicated vs Hosted recommendations for joint accounts, and aligning on a pilot for a retail customer. Actionable next steps, who owns what, and a follow-up pipeline sprint scheduled.

Topics:
- Playbook gaps: intake, lead tagging, crediting
- Technical constraints: VPC/Dedicated, regional capacity, KV cache and cold-starts
- Commercials: referral credit, co-sell revenue split, pricing guardrails
- Risk triage: security questionnaires, SOC 2, data residency

Transcript Body:
[00:00:00] Jordan Li: "Alright everyone, thanks for carving out time. I know this is a lot on a Tuesday afternoon so we'll try to keep it tight. Quick round of intros — Jordan from Redwood, Maya our SE, Carlos on partners — and over to Priya to do a quick framing from Oceanic. Priya?"
[00:00:12] Priya Nair: "Yep, hi all. Thanks. I wanted this to be less of a deck read and more of a what worked/what didn't, so we can iterate the co-sell play. We've got a few deals that stalled and I want to understand the frictions. Mainly intake and the crediting question — like who gets motion credit when we bring the lead."
[00:00:30] Ethan Morales: "Yeah, and also clarity on which accounts we should push to Dedicated vs Hosted — finance keeps asking about committed MRR thresholds before they sign onto Dedicated pools."
[00:00:42] Maya Patel: "Totally. On the tech side we've seen a few surprise asks — like customers wanting VPC egress and on-prem options concurrently. For the RetailPilot prospect, there's some sequence-length concerns because of long context windows; that affects kernel choices and cost. Our recommended path there is Dedicated with quantization profile Q4-lite, but I know cost is sensitive."
[00:01:05] Dr. Lena Zhou: "Can I just flag, we got one security questionnaire item asking about KMS/HSM rotations and audit logs. Our legal wants explicit mention of HSM-backed key management and per-request auditability. Is that baked into the Private offering?"
[00:01:20] Carlos Mendes: "Short answer: yes, Private and Dedicated both support KMS integrations; we do have HSM options for enterprise. But we should make it clearer in the playbook so partners don't get surprised and ping the SE last minute."
[00:01:33] Jordan Li: "That's one of the playbook gaps — we didn't put the security checklist early enough in the intake flow. Priya, if we add a checkbox and doc link at the partner intake step, would that help?"
[00:01:42] Priya Nair: "Yes, that would help a lot. Also, the current intake form doesn't pipe leads into your CRM with a partner tag reliably — Ethan saw some leads fall through the cracks."
[00:01:52] Ethan Morales: "Yeah I exported the pipeline and filtered for partner-source shows blank for some rows; I think the UTM / source param mapping isn't hooked. Carlos, you mentioned a tagging spec?"
[00:02:03] Carlos Mendes: "I started a draft last week. I'll consolidate it and flag mandatory fields: partner_id, partner_contact_email, referral_date, co_sell_enablement_flag. We'll share it after this call.
[00:02:12] Speaker 1 (transcript artifact): "Mhm um yeah""
[00:02:18] Maya Patel: "On the pilot scoping — RetailPilot has the biggest risk being latency spikes during batch reprice windows. We should propose request routing: read-heavy queries to hosted edge, heavy generation to Dedicated with fallback to a smaller hosted model to avoid user-visible errors."
[00:02:40] Amir Khan: "So we'd be mixing runtimes. Is the KV cache compatible across hosted and dedicated instances? We don't want cold-starts thrashing the cache on a per-region basis."
[00:02:51] Maya Patel: "There is prefix/KV cache sharing but it's not automatic across tenancy boundaries. We'd need to architect a shared cache or accept a warm-up period. In practice, for low-latency windows we keep the hot shards on Dedicated and route by policy. Sorry, the transcript picks 'K V cache' sometimes — SE lazymode."
[00:03:12] Jordan Li: "That means some upfront engineering in the pilot to pin top templates and pre-warm the cache. Maya can outline the runbook and the estimated eng hours. Maya?"
[00:03:21] Maya Patel: "I can, I'll map it. Roughly 2-3 eng days to wire pre-warm and a day to validate routing policies per region. If we need HSM key rotations tied to deploys it's another day. We'll call out the days in the runbook."
[00:03:33] Priya Nair: "From the partner ops perspective we care about the co-sell crediting. Some of our sales folks are nervous that if Redwood claims platform credit, Oceanic loses commission. We need a clear revenue share example in the playbook that maps to SFDC opportunities."
[00:03:49] Jordan Li: "We can build a table: partner-sourced, partner-assisted, partner-led — with % revenue share and who owns the renewal. But legal will need to sign off. Carlos, can you take the lead on that?"
[00:03:58] Carlos Mendes: "Yep, I'll propose a default split model and a waiver path for special enterprise deals. I'll also write a short legal blurb that the partner-facing AE can send."
[00:04:08] [00:04:08] Speaker 2: "Uh huh""
[00:04:12] Ethan Morales: "One more ops point — pricing. Our procurement team asked for 'guardrails' so our AE's don't lowball. Can you provide recommended list prices and discount bands for co-sell deals?"
[00:04:23] Jordan Li: "Yes, we'll add a pricing matrix: suggested MSRP, typical discount ranges by commit size, and example math for token-based pricing vs committed throughput. For Dedicated, we'll show committed GPU hour equivalents so Finance can map to MRR. I'll send an editable sheet."
[00:04:38] Priya Nair: "Perfect. Also, a small thing: some customers inquire about single-tenant data residency in EU. Is there a region-limited Dedicated offering or a Private deploy example?"
[00:04:49] Maya Patel: "We have Dedicated capacity in EU-west and we can do Private in EMEA via our on-prem appliance or via partner-hosted VPC. We'll add a region decision tree to the playbook."
[00:05:02] Dr. Lena Zhou: "Okay good. On the technical deep-dive side — we want to ensure model equivalence. When you route to hosted fallback models, how do you control hallucination rates? We found another vendor's fallback had wildly different tokenization which altered outputs."
[00:05:17] Maya Patel: "We recommend fallback models that are architecture-compatible — quantization and tokenizer parity is part of the onboarding checklist. We'll include quality thresholds and acceptance tests (bleu/bertscore-ish and prompt-based evals)."
[00:05:31] Jordan Li: "This is where Redwood Optimize can help — detect regressions tied to a prompt set and alert. We'll surface a small eval harness in the playbook for partners to run quickly."
[00:05:42] Priya Nair: "Good. A lot of this is operational — intake, tagging, runbooks, and the pricing matrix. If we can get those in a 1-pager playbook, that becomes our 'partner cheat-sheet' and should reduce back-and-forth."
[00:05:56] Jordan Li: "Agreed. We'll do a 1-pager plus an extended playbook. Quick check: what's the ideal cadence for Pipeline sprints?"
[00:06:06] Priya Nair: "Bi-weekly is my preference initially; then we can move to monthly when the process is stable. The first sprint should be hands-on with top-5 accounts."
[00:06:15] Carlos Mendes: "Let's do a 30-minute kickoff and then 60-minute deep dives for each account. I'll coordinate slots in October — week of the 13th looks promising for both teams.
[00:06:26] Speaker 3 (partial): "Mm-hmm""
[00:06:32] Ethan Morales: "On the legal side — we have a question about co-sell attribution in our SFDC. Do you prefer a partner-defined field or do you want Redwood to stamp opportunities? We need to avoid duplicate ownership issues."
[00:06:44] Jordan Li: "Best is partner-defined field so Oceanic controls tagging; Redwood will consume it via an agreed mapping. That avoids retroactive disputes. We'll send a mapping doc. Carlos will own that."
[00:06:54] Priya Nair: "One sticky objection: some of our sales team voiced that Redwood's Dedicated commitment lengths are too long (12 months) for smaller deals. Is there a smaller, monthly-billable Dedicated tier?"
[00:07:07] Maya Patel: "We do offer burst and micro-commitments in some regions for pilot accounts, but it's limited. For pilots we can do a 3-month pilot with pro-rated dedicated pool and then convert. I'll document the pilot template."
[00:07:20] Amir Khan: "From a solutions standpoint, we also need guidance on sizing: concurrency vs tokens-per-second. Our app has spiky concurrency around noon; what's the best approach?"
[00:07:30] Maya Patel: "Size for 95th-percentile RPS for Dedicated; use request-level autoscaling policies and overflow to hosted capacity for bursts. Batching helps lower cost but watch latency. We'll provide a sizing worksheet."
[00:07:42] Jordan Li: "Okay let's pivot to deal-level triage — quick run through of top joint opportunities. Priya, can you list them?"
[00:07:50] Priya Nair: "Yes — RetailPilot (high priority), FinServe (mid), GreenLogistics (early), MediaPlus (won't pursue this quarter), and HealthGrid (security-heavy)."
[00:08:02] Jordan Li: "RetailPilot — status?"
[00:08:04] Ethan Morales: "We have an inbound POC ask, security questionnaire in progress. They want an SLA and VPC. Pricing is the blocker — they expect sub-$X per 1k tokens equivalent, which is tight."
[00:08:17] Maya Patel: "We can propose Dedicated with a pilot discount; ensure we set a guardrail so the discount doesn't set long-term expectations. Use a timeboxed pilot with success criteria: latency < 150ms p95 for reads and under Y cost per call."
[00:08:33] Priya Nair: "Who will run the pilot -- Redwood or Oceanic? We need clarity on operational ownership."
[00:08:38] Jordan Li: "Joint run: Redwood SE leads infra setup, Oceanic handles customer relations and demo. We'll include a runbook with named owners."
[00:08:46] [00:08:46] Speaker 4 (auto): "Okay""
[00:08:49] Dr. Lena Zhou: "For FinServe and HealthGrid, security review will be long. Does Redwood have red-team or penetration test reports we can share?"
[00:08:58] Carlos Mendes: "Yes, we have pen test artifacts and SOC2 Type II. I'll attach the security bundle to the playbook and also the redacted pen test summary for customers."
[00:09:09] Priya Nair: "Awesome. A small request — can you add a quick one-liner per account on which Redwood product to recommend? e.g., Hosted for MediaPlus, Dedicated for RetailPilot, Private for HealthGrid?"
[00:09:20] Jordan Li: "Yes, we'll add a one-line recommendation and rationale per account. Good idea.
[00:09:26] Maya Patel: "Also, for HealthGrid we need a data residency map — some PHI constraints. Private deploy is the default ask there, but we can sometimes do dedicated in a single-tenant VPC if legal accepts it."
[00:09:39] Ethan Morales: "One ops hiccup I've seen: the joint lead handoff doc isn't enforced. Sometimes Redwood AEs start outreach without letting Oceanic prep the customer. We need a minimal SLA: 48 hours heads-up before any outbound outreach."
[00:09:52] Priya Nair: "Yes please. We lost one lead to an unsynced outreach which messed the relationship. 48-hour heads up is reasonable."
[00:09:58] Jordan Li: "We agree. We'll put a partner coordination SLA in the intake doc.
[00:10:03] [00:10:03] Speaker 2: "Mm""
[00:10:07] Jordan Li: "Any other major frictions we should cover?"
[00:10:09] Priya Nair: "One last one — enablement. Some of our reps want quick product cheat sheets and sample demos they can use in pitch meetings. A short video would be ideal."
[00:10:18] Carlos Mendes: "We can produce a 6-minute demo vid + 2-page cheat sheet. I'll work with DX to push it out."
[00:10:25] Jordan Li: "Great. Let's confirm owners and then recap next steps."

Recap (spoken):
[00:10:30] Jordan Li: "Recap: Carlos will produce partner intake tagging spec and legal blurb (due Oct 6). Maya will produce the pilot technical runbook and pilot template (due Oct 7). Jordan will send pricing matrix and updated co-sell one-pager (due Oct 3). Priya to share top-8 accounts (due Oct 2). We'll schedule pipeline sprint week of Oct 13. Any objections?"
[00:10:55] Priya Nair: "No objections — sounds good. This is much clearer than before.
[00:11:00] Ethan Morales: "I'll follow up with the SFDC export and flag the problematic rows. Thanks all."
[00:11:06] Dr. Lena Zhou: "Thanks. Appreciate the quick turnaround on the security artifacts.
[00:11:10] Jordan Li: "Thanks everyone — we'll be in touch.
